Watching late-week snow potential after amazing Veterans’ Day

By
Tanner Beam
-
November 10, 2026 11:40 pm
Share
Facebook
X
Print
Email
Pinterest
ReddIt
Viber
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 1:58
    Instaread

    Overall, a nice Tuesday greeted us across the region and and we will have one more nice day before we have rain and snow moving into the area with a low pressure system. Looking at the European model, rain will move into the region early in the day on Thursday and should last with us in some areas through most of Thursday. It shouldn’t be a total washout, but heavy rain does appear to fall at times. The real fun begins as we look ahead to Friday.

    CheckForecasts

    Snowflakes look to make their appearance known on Friday. Rain will transition to snow late in the night Thursday across parts of Pocahontas County before most of the area transitions on Friday. The European model is trending much drier than the GFS model and doesn’t have much snow accumulating across the area. Again, this is all going to be very dependent on the amount of snow that falls, how quick it cools the ground down and how long it ends up lasting across the area. Football games on Friday look to be on the snowy and cold side, especially for those in Meadow Bridge. Make sure to bring a nice coat and gloves to the games because it sure will be cold!

    Looking at the full 7 day forecast; temperatures will drop off rapidly behind the cold front on Thursday and will lead to rain changing over to snow for most as we head into Friday. The GFS and European model still do not agree on the snowfall totals and a the cooling of the ground will be the key component as to where the snow truly accumulates. That appears most likely in the highest elevation areas across Pocahontas and Greenbrier Counties. We will start to warm up closer to average as we head into next week. Temperatures also tank into the mid 20’s going into Sunday and Monday mornings.
